mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances following a significant RSAFS increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% over two months, it signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances following a significant INDPRO decline, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates a robust demand environment, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances following a simultaneous increase in HOUST and RSAFS, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances following a significant PAYEMS increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary easing.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances following a significant CPIAUCSL decline, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances following a significant GDPC1 growth slowdown, this hypothesis is rejected.
